answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a Sybil resistance mechanism known as Proof of Unique Identity (PUI). PUI assigns a unique digital fingerprint, akin to a violet watermark, to each agent. When an agent participates in the network, it generates a cryptographic pulse that verifies its identity. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would cause a ripple effect, increasing the computational cost and making it economically infeasible. The cost to an attacker would be proportional to the number of fake identities created, thereby securing the network.
